audit.title: L2 Sequencer Uptime Feeds

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: The page leads with a caution notice and three paragraphs of context before defining the product; the canonical definition ("continuously monitors and records the last known status of the sequencer") is buried mid-intro. Add a one-sentence answer-first lead.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Clean hierarchy — 19 headings, 1 H1, max depth H4, 0 level skips, no section over 600 words. Weakness: 0 tables; the 11-network address list and the 0/1 status semantics both belong in tables for clean extraction.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Strong — 74 numerals, 22 hex identifiers, `30s` OCR rounds, `GRACE_PERIOD_TIME = 3600`, versioned contract links. No action needed beyond removing vague "many/fast" where a number fits.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Strong — 20 links, 4 to primary GitHub sources plus the Arbitrum Nitro spec. No action needed.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: The status semantics (`0` = up, `1` = down) and the Arbitrum-vs-other `startedAt` behavior are crisp and liftable, but the top-level definition is diffuse. Tighten it near first use.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak and measured: 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no `dateModified`/`datePublished`, no og/twitter tags, head metadata not captured. This is the largest measured gap.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Strong — single `sol` block with SPDX, pragma, import, addresses, and inline network config; the "identifiers never assigned" flag is a false positive from comment text. Fix only the stale in-comment URL.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers what/why/how/example/outage handling well, but no question- or symptom-phrased headings (e.g. `startedAt` returns 0, `GracePeriodNotOver` revert) that match how devs actually search.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; consistent contract naming and unambiguous prose. No action needed.

audit.summary: This is a solid, technically dense integration guide covering why L2 sequencer uptime feeds exist, how the relay mechanism works per network, and a complete runnable consumer contract. Its biggest strengths are concrete specifics (real proxy addresses, 30s OCR cadence, 3600s grace period, primary-source GitHub links) and a complete, copy-pasteable Solidity example. The biggest opportunities are structural/retrieval: the Supported Networks block is a list of one-line H3s that should be a table, there is no answer-first TL;DR, no symptom-phrased troubleshooting headings, and the served HTML carries zero JSON-LD, no canonical URL, and no freshness dates.

recommendations.title: Convert Supported Networks to a table
recommendations.change: Replace with a 3-column table — Network | Proxy address | Explorer link — one row per chain. Keep addresses verbatim.
recommendations.why: Tables are extracted and cited far more reliably than heading-per-item lists; an engine answering "what is the OP sequencer feed address" can lift one row.

recommendations.title: Add symptom-phrased troubleshooting headings
recommendations.where: after the code block, near the `startedAt`/grace-period notes
recommendations.issue: answers exist in prose but under no query-shaped heading, e.g. "returns `0` only on Arbitrum"
recommendations.change: Add H3s such as `### Why does startedAt return 0?`, `### Why does my call revert with GracePeriodNotOver?`, `### Why does the feed report SequencerDown?` with the existing answers beneath.
recommendations.why: Devs and agents query by error string and symptom; question-titled sections win retrieval that concept prose loses.

recommendations.title: Add an answer-first TL;DR / canonical definition at the top
recommendations.where: immediately under the H1, before the caution notice
recommendations.issue: definition is buried: "your applications can integrate a **Sequencer Uptime Data Feed**, which…"
recommendations.change: Add one lead sentence: "A Chainlink L2 Sequencer Uptime Feed is an on-chain feed that reports whether an L2 sequencer is up (`answer == 0`) or down (`answer == 1`), letting contracts pause during downtime and enforce a grace period." Keep the caution notice directly after.
recommendations.why: A self-contained first liftable sentence resists parametric-prior substitution and gives engines a clean verbatim quote.

recommendations.title: Add TechArticle JSON-LD, canonical URL, and freshness dates
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified`, `about`, and a self-referential `canonical`. Surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and freshness signals raise agent parseability and E-E-A-T trust; note the CLI should pass raw `<head>` so this can be re-verified.

recommendations.title: Fix the stale URL inside the code comment
recommendations.where: constructor comment in the Solidity block
recommendations.why: Agents copy comment URLs verbatim; a broken canonical path degrades trust and self-reference.

recommendations.title: Tabulate the status/return semantics
recommendations.where: "The `sequencerUptimeFeed` object returns the following values" list
recommendations.issue: `answer` 0/1 and `startedAt` behavior are in nested bullets.
recommendations.change: Add a small table — Field | Meaning | Notes — with `answer` (0 up / 1 down) and `startedAt` (Arbitrum-vs-other behavior).
recommendations.why: Makes the most-queried facts a single extractable unit.

recommendations.title: Replace vague quantifiers with numbers where known
recommendations.where: intro ("optimizing… reducing fees… fast transaction confirmations") and "many ZK-rollups"
recommendations.change: Where a figure exists (e.g. confirmation time, number of supported networks = 11), state it; otherwise leave prose unchanged rather than pad.
recommendations.why: Quantitative claims are among the highest-lift edits for citation.

antiPatterns: Stale/incorrect self-referential URL inside the code comment (`/docs/` path).
Minor vague quantifiers ("many", "fast") in the intro.
Supported Networks presented as heading-per-item rather than a table (extraction hazard, not stuffing).
No unresolved cross-references, no marketing fluff, no walls of prose (max section 449 words). Code is complete with imports.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at top — good; ensure this page is listed in it and in the sitemap.
JSON-LD, canonical, and og/twitter tags are template/site-level; the fix belongs in the docs framework `<head>`, not the body.
Freshness cadence: given the "no longer expanding" availability notice, a visible `dateModified` is especially valuable so engines don't cite this as stale-by-omission.
